passage:
During repairs at an old train station, workers found a wall painting hidden behind layers of paint. It showed mountains, farms, and a train moving through a valley.
The station office wanted to remove it because the wall needed work. Local residents disagreed. Some remembered seeing the painting when they were children. Others said it told the story of the town before factories came.
Experts were called to clean and protect the painting. The repair took longer and cost more, but the station became a place people visited, not only passed through.
A wall can hold more than bricks and paint. It can hold the memory of what a place once believed about itself.
